title: Quantum Kernels are Spectral Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum kernels admit Fourier representations whose frequencies are determined by the data-encoding gates of the underlying feature map. We show that entangling tensor kernels are matrix product operator factorizations of the corresponding Fourier coefficient tensors, thereby identifying quantum kernels as spectral tensor networks. By grouping gate-level frequency configurations that yield the same feature-wise frequency, we obtain a grouped Fourier form that induces a more compact spectral tensor network representation of the kernel. We further show that kernel target alignment serves as a bridge between the Fourier and tensor network views. On a grid that resolves the accessible Fourier modes, it becomes the Frobenius cosine similarity between Fourier coefficient tensors. Our numerical experiments show that layered quantum kernels admit accurate representations with small bond dimension, revealing a compressibility governed by correlations between Fourier modes. This compressibility provides a diagnostic of classical representability and of whether kernel evaluation is likely to remain classically tractable.
summary: This paper proves that quantum kernels can be mathematically recast as spectral tensor networks by analyzing their Fourier representations. It introduces Kernel Target Alignment (KTA) and measures the resulting 'spectral compressibility' using bond dimensions. This provides a diagnostic tool to determine if evaluating a quantum kernel is likely to remain classically tractable.
main_problem: The core problem is identifying quantum kernels, derived from feature maps, as spectral tensor networks to understand their computational complexity.
main_result: Quantum kernels can be exactly represented by spectral tensor networks, and the compressibility of their Fourier coefficient tensors serves as a diagnostic for classical tractability.
method: The authors use Fourier analysis to decompose quantum kernels into coefficients ($	ilde{c}_{\omega,\omega'}$), which are then mapped onto Matrix Product Operator (MPO) factorizations characteristic of spectral tensor networks.
model_or_system: The model involves quantum feature states $|\Phi(x)angle$ generated by layered data-encoding quantum circuits. The kernel is $\kappa(x, x') = |\langle\Phi(x)|\Phi(x')angle|^2$.
key_observables: Spectral compressibility (rank structure of Fourier coefficients), Bond Dimension ($\chi$), and Kernel Target Alignment (KTA).
important_parameters: Bond dimension ($\chi$), circuit depth ($L$), and the frequency-resolving grid ($\mathcal{G}\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on assuming a specific structure for data-encoding gates and utilizing the approximation that KTA simplifies to the Frobenius cosine similarity on a frequency-resolving grid.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition from quantum feature maps to spectral tensor networks using $\hat{C}$, compare gate-level vs. feature-wise scaling, and show KTA converging to unity as bond dimension increases.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing identities linking Fourier expansions to ETK contractions, deriving a compact grouped Fourier form, defining KTA as the bridge metric, and finally using numerical experiments to demonstrate spectral compressibility diagnostics.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful mathematical tool (tensor networks) to analyze quantum information processing tasks (kernel methods), offering a concrete measure of when quantum computation might be classically simulable.
